newsitem.title: USA: Warner-Lambert sees sales, EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Warner-Lambert sees sales, EPS growth.

text.p: Warner-Lambert Co said Tuesday it expects on average to post double-digit increases in sales and mid-teens growth in earnings through the end of the decade.

The projection is based in part on new pharmaceutical products being developed and introduced, including Lipitor, a cholesterol reducer, it said. In addition, the company said it expects to get approval for Rezulin, a treatment for type II diabetes.

"As a result of the successful discovery and development of innovative new products, we believe Warner-Lambert is poised to enter a sustained period of unprecedented growth," Chairman and Chief Executive Melvin Goodes said in a statement.
However, the company said its 1996 results were hurt by foreign exchange rates, which dropped sales by three percent.

For 1996, the company reported net income of $786.5 million, or $2.90 per share, on sales of $7.23 billion. For the prior year, it reported net income of $739.5 million, or $2.74 per share, on sales of $7.04 billion.
